title: Customer Impact Deck Templates — Flex + Enterprise
summary: Two adaptable QBR deck outlines (Flex / Enterprise) plus slide-level speaker notes, a lightweight renewal ask framework, and a simple textual renewal tracker that can be pasted into a spreadsheet. Designed for CS teams that need a single source-of-truth deck that can be right-sized quickly for mid-market vs. strategic accounts.
content:
Purpose and guidance:
- Goal: Help CSMs run concise, outcome-oriented QBRs that surface technical health, usage patterns, ROI signals, and a clear renewal/next-steps pathway.
- When to use: Standard "Flex" for most customers (30–40 minute total). Enterprise variant for strategic/exec-level reviews (60+ minutes) with deeper technical appendix.
- Notes to self: this is a living doc — iterate with Solutions Eng after two pilots (accounts: BrightPath, CobaltRetail). Link outcomes back to adoption playbooks in Confluence (CONFL-11234).

High-level templates (slide order, bullets):

1) Flex (30–40 min; single-deck):
  - Cover (1): Customer name, date, CSM, renewal window (MM/YYYY), one-line meeting objective.
  - Executive snapshot (1): Top 3 business outcomes we enabled / top 3 risks; simple 60s talking points.
  - Adoption snapshot (1): Active users, API calls/day, core feature adoption heatmap (bullets).
  - Performance & reliability (1): P95 latency, error rate trend, recent incidents & mitigations (last 90 days).
  - Value realized (2): Highlight 2–3 use cases with metrics (e.g., reduced support deflection by X%, summarization throughput). Include short customer quote if available.
  - Cost & efficiency (1): Unit economics snapshot, suggested optimizations (batching, quantization), expected impact.
  - Risks & needs (1): Current blockers (integration gaps, latency-sensitive routes, compliance needs).
  - Renewal ask & options (1): Renewal window, recommended package, one-click asks (upgrade, add seats, add Dedicated).
  - Action plan & owners (1): 30/60/90 day commitments with owners and delivery dates.
  - Appendix & next steps (1): Links to runbooks, evals, and technical contacts.

Speaker notes (Flex):
  - Exec snapshot: Keep to one slide; lead with business outcome first. e.g., "In Q4 we helped reduce routing latency for X, enabling a faster checkout flow — expected to increase conversion by Y%."
  - Technical health: Call out whether observed latency is due to model choice, token length, or infra. Use simple flagging: Green/Amber/Red.
  - Renewal ask: Always present 2 options (conservative + expanded) and include expected ROI for each.

2) Enterprise (60+ min; executive + technical):
  - Cover (1): Expanded with exec logos, tailored objectives, and legal renewal window.
  - Executive narrative (2): Business context, strategic initiatives where Redwood sits, impact roadmap.
  - Adoption deep-dive (2): Segment usage by team/product, growth curves, churn/retention signals.
  - Technical health & SLAs (2–3): P99/P95 trends, capacity headroom, KV cache hit rate, quantization parity. Include incident postmortems summary (if relevant).
  - Security & compliance posture (1): KMS/HSM status, audit log highlights, on-prem connector state.
  - Cost optimization scenarios (1–2): Modeled options (e.g., Dedicated with burst vs. Hosted premium) with cost and latency tradeoffs.
  - Customer roadmap alignment (1): Joint milestones, integration dependencies, cross-team owners.
  - Renewal proposal (1): Detailed term options, suggested incentives, legal points to escalate.
  - Technical appendix (multiple): Model configs, latency traces, perf graphs, PRs referencing optimizations.

Speaker notes (Enterprise):
  - For execs: Start with outcomes tied to the customer P&L or OKRs. Keep technical slides for the engineers afterwards.
  - For SRE/Infra: prepare 5-min brief on capacity plan and fallback/policy routing.
  - For procurement/legal: have one slide with billing cadence, minimum commitments, and SLOs.

Renewal ask frameworks (text snippets to paste into slide):
- Conservative (renew-as-is): "We recommend a 12-month renewal at current tier to maintain continuity while we deliver on roadmap items A and B. Expected uplift: maintain current SLA and avoid migration work."
- Growth (expand seats/capacity): "Recommend +20% units and a 6-month pilot of Dedicated capacity for route X. Expected latency reduction: 30–40% for critical endpoints; estimated cost delta: $Y/month."
- Strategic (co-sell/partner): "Propose an enterprise partnership: co-marketing + product integration for a 24-month term; include premium SLAs and roadmap commitments."

Risk signaling guide (one-liner rules):
- Green: Usage up or steady; no open high-severity issues; ROI signals present.
- Amber: One or more moderate issues (integration friction, rising error rate), adoption stalled but fixable.
- Red: Contract at risk (low usage, unresolved technical barriers, exec disengagement).

Lightweight renewal tracker (paste into sheet):
- Columns: account_id, account_name, csm, renewal_window, current_tier, recommended_option, estimated_annual_delta, risk_flag, next_step_owner, next_step_date, notes
- Example row (CSV text):
  10023,BrightPath,Aisha Patel,2025-07,Standard,Growth,+$42,000,Amber,Marco Hernandez,2025-03-15,"Schedule Dedicated pilot kickoff;DEP-43"

Actionable playbook snippets (CS workflow):
- 8 weeks out: Run adoption & billing audit, request exec alignment call. (owner: CSM)
- 6 weeks out: Send renewal options, cost/ROI brief (owner: AE/CSM).
- 4 weeks out: Execute commercial negotiation; escalate to GTM leadership if customer requests >20% discount. (owner: AE)
- 2 weeks out: Finalize contract language, collect PO if needed, confirm onboarding dates for expanded capacity. (owner: Sales Ops)

Customization checklist (for CSM prepping the deck):
- Replace placeholders: metrics, customer quotes, logos.
- Attach 2–4 customer-specific case studies (one-pagers).
- Validate perf metrics against telemetry: confirm P95 values and error counts with Observability team (ticket: OBS-339).
- Add specific legal/licensing constraints if on Private deployment.

Appendix suggestions (copyable):
- Runbook links
  - On-call contact: eng-sre@redwood.com
  - Incident history (last 90 days): LINK_TO_INCIDENT_LOG
  - Integration checklist: CONFL-12200
- Technical artifacts to attach: latency CSV, core model config, example prompt sets, eval results (diff vs. baseline).

Unresolved questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Pilot this with two strategic customers in March — capture feedback on "Enterprise" slide density.
- Coordinate with Solutions Eng to produce 1-page Dedicated pilot cost model template.
- Confirm legal template options for 24-month partnership discounts. (legal owner: Elena Kim).

Quick-copy items for in-slide CTAs:
- "Approve pilot" (button/ask) — owner: CSM; deadline: 2 weeks.
- "Schedule technical kickoff" — owner: Solutions Eng; deadline: 5 business days.

Sample email follow-up (post-QBR):
Subject: QBR recap & next steps — [Customer] — [Date]
Hi [Name],
Thanks for the time today. Attached is the deck from our QBR and the 30/60/90 action plan we agreed on. Key next steps:
- Dedicated pilot kickoff (Marco) — target: [date]
- Contract option selection (AE) — target: [date]
Please reply with any clarifying questions — we’ll update the tracker once items are scheduled.
Thanks,
Aisha

Editable deliverables to attach when sharing: one-slide renewal options, 1-page Dedicated cost model, 30/60/90 action plan template (CSV), appendix bundle (logs + perf).

Last checked: 2025-02-16 by Aisha Patel.
Feedback loop: Add comments in this doc or drop a note in #cs-qbr-templates.
